title: File Handling: Opening, Reading, Writing, and Resource Management
description: How opening, reading, writing, and closing files compares across the three languages, especially resource cleanup.

content.heading: Python
content.body: open(path, mode) returns a file object; with open(...) as f: guarantees f.close() runs automatically, even on an exception. read()/readline()/readlines() and write()/writelines() cover text and (with a "b" mode) binary data. Encoding is explicit and configurable (encoding="utf-8").

content.heading: Java
content.body: Multiple APIs exist: the older java.io (FileReader/FileWriter, BufferedReader/BufferedWriter) and the more modern java.nio.file (Path, Files, with convenience methods like Files.readString()). try-with-resources guarantees any AutoCloseable resource (including file streams) is closed automatically, mirroring Python's with statement.

content.heading: C
content.body: FILE *fp = fopen(path, mode); returns a FILE pointer, or NULL on failure (which must be checked manually — nothing does this automatically). fprintf/fscanf, fgets/fputs, and fread/fwrite handle text and binary I/O. fclose(fp) must be called explicitly by the programmer; there is no with-style or try-with-resources-style automatic cleanup mechanism — forgetting fclose() is a real, easy-to-make mistake with no language-level safety net.

content.heading: Key Differences
content.body: Python's with and Java's try-with-resources both guarantee cleanup automatically, even across exceptions; C requires manually calling fclose() on every code path, including every early-return error path, with nothing enforcing this — a forgotten fclose() simply leaks the file handle (and possibly unflushed data) with no warning.

content.heading: When It Matters
content.body: This resource-cleanup guarantee is a genuinely significant reliability difference: Python and Java code is far less prone to resource leaks from a forgotten cleanup call, especially on exception/error paths, compared to equivalent C code that must get every fclose() right by hand, on every path, every time.

keyPoints: Python's with and Java's try-with-resources both guarantee automatic file cleanup, even on exceptions
C requires manual fopen()/fclose() pairing with no automatic cleanup mechanism at all
All three provide both text and binary I/O, but only C requires the programmer to check fopen()'s NULL return manually
